prompt.context: Our client, GridMask, is a software company that for the last two years has focused on developing face-detecting systems. The technology is ready to be deployed in 2017 and the company is looking at ways to sell it — for instance, to provide payment authorization, access to facilities, or assist authorities in tracking down criminals. The client has hired us to (1) identify the best revenue streams to focus on, and (2) strengthen venture capitalists' perception of market feasibility for potential new rounds of financing.
prompt.question: Which revenue streams should GridMask prioritize, and how would you frame the investment narrative for potential venture capital investors?

clarifying_info.q: How has the company financed operations over the past two years?
clarifying_info.a: GridMask covered all its expenses with venture funds and can fully operate until the end of 2016 without needing additional money.

clarifying_info.q: Did GridMask generate any revenue during its development phase?
clarifying_info.a: They only had negligible revenue streams in the past years from small consulting projects.

clarifying_info.q: When does the company expect to become self-sustaining?
clarifying_info.a: They have identified that they can start generating revenue to sustain their operations a year from now (2018 — just before depleting their current budget).

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors in this space?
clarifying_info.a: There is one more company already offering a similar but very inferior finished alternative.

exhibits.title: Income & Revenue Streams
exhibits.shows: Selected income statements for GridMask (in millions of USD) for 2016, 2017 expected, and 2018 expected; plus a chart of identified opportunities across all potential client segments showing risk/reward trade-offs and competitor market share

data.note: Expected 2017 and 2018 statements assume distributing selling efforts across all identified markets with the same level of marketing efforts

Access_to_Facilities.characterization: large untapped market, low competitor penetration

framework: Understand current financial position and runway
Analyze projected income statements to assess path to profitability
Evaluate each revenue stream by market size, competitor presence, and strategic fit
Identify which revenue streams maximize growth while managing competitive risk
Craft VC narrative: highlight 2018 operating profit inflection and strategic focus

questions.prompt: Analyze the income statements. What do they reveal about GridMask's financial health and the urgency of new financing?
questions.guidance: A strong answer notes that 2016 and 2017 show operating losses (-3.3M and -3.8M respectively), meaning the company is burning cash. The 2017 expected statement assumes equal marketing effort across all markets. The critical insight is the sharp jump to +7.1M operating profit in 2018, but this is conditional on successfully deploying revenue streams. The candidate should flag that the company needs bridge funding through 2017 to reach the 2018 inflection point.

math.setup: Compare operating profit trajectory: 2016 actual vs. 2017 vs. 2018 expected
math.answer: The company swings from -3.8M in 2017 to +7.1M in 2018 — a ~700% revenue jump and immediate positive ROI once the first clients are secured. However, the 2017 gap requires VC bridging.

questions.prompt: Which revenue stream should GridMask prioritize and why?
questions.guidance: A strong answer uses the right panel of Exhibit 1 to compare the three streams: (1) Payment Authorization is the largest market but competitor holds 87% share — too entrenched for a new entrant; (2) Access to Facilities has a large untapped market with only 18% competitor penetration — best balance of size and opportunity; (3) Criminal Tracking is a smaller, stable government-contract market but carries reputational/privacy risk. The recommended priority order is Access to Facilities first (best risk/reward), followed by selectively pursuing Payment Authorization if the product is demonstrably superior, while using Criminal Tracking as a stable revenue base with caution.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors should GridMask consider when evaluating each revenue stream?

categories.name: Market attractiveness
ideas: Pricing power vs. willingness to pay

categories.name: Competitive dynamics
ideas: Competitor's existing market share (87% in Payment Auth vs. 18% in Facilities)
Quality gap between GridMask and competitor
Risk of competitor response or price war
Switching costs for existing customers of competitor

categories.name: Strategic fit
ideas: Alignment with GridMask's core technology strengths
Speed to revenue given 2017 cash burn
Sales cycle length (government vs. enterprise vs. payments)

categories.name: Risk factors
ideas: Regulatory risk in criminal tracking / privacy concerns
Reputational risk of association with surveillance
Dependency on a single large client
Price point vs. competitor — unknown relative positioning

categories.name: VC narrative levers
ideas: Show focused go-to-market rather than spreading efforts equally
Demonstrate product superiority over the one existing competitor
Quantify market share capture scenario in Access to Facilities

recommendation: GridMask should prioritize 'Access to Facilities' as its primary revenue stream — it offers the largest untapped market with only 18% competitor penetration, giving GridMask the best opportunity to establish a strong initial position.

'Payment Authorization' is the largest market but the competitor holds 87% share; GridMask should pursue it only if it can clearly demonstrate superior product quality sufficient to displace an entrenched player.

'Criminal Tracking' offers stable government contracts but is a limited market and carries privacy/reputational risk that could disadvantage GridMask even against an inferior competitor; treat as secondary.
The VC narrative should center on the 2018 operating profit inflection (+7.1M), the focused go-to-market strategy (not spreading equally), and the product quality advantage over the sole competitor.
Securing bridge funding through 2017 (-3.8M gap) is critical; the ROI is nearly immediate once first client contracts are signed in 2018.
risks: Competitor retaliates aggressively in Access to Facilities once GridMask enters
GridMask's price point is unknown relative to market demand — could materially affect revenue projections
Equal distribution of marketing efforts (the assumption behind 2018 forecast) may not be optimal; focused investment could accelerate or alter the numbers
Criminal Tracking associations with surveillance could taint brand in other segments
2018 projections carry execution risk — first client acquisition may take longer than modeled
next_steps: Conduct competitive benchmarking to quantify GridMask's product quality advantage over the competitor
Determine optimal pricing strategy relative to competitor and market willingness-to-pay
Develop a focused go-to-market plan weighted toward Access to Facilities
Model alternative revenue scenarios (focused vs. spread) to stress-test the 2018 forecast
Prepare VC pitch deck anchored on 2018 inflection, focused strategy, and competitive differentiation
